text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a pediatric patient presenting with a limp and localized pain, but no fever or acute distress. To better understand your condition, could you tell me exactly where it hurts and how long you have had this limp?

text: 7-year-old male. Mother has noticed a change in the child’s play patterns, specifically favoring his left leg while walking or running. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease (Avascular Necrosis of the Femoral Head).

The presentation of a limp and localized left knee pain in a 7-year-old male without fever or trauma is classic for this condition, as the hip pathology often refers pain to the knee. I have reached my diagnostic conclusion based on the history provided.
